chapter: Cotton Club and radio fame with Cab
title: Big Broadcast of 1934 and Bing Crosby at the Paramount
summary: Mills gets the band the Bing Crosby film; Thomas recalls playing the Paramount with Bing as extra attraction and Cab's friction with Bing's brother.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: And another thing... I don't know whether that happened later. Because see, Mills got us a job to do the first picture with Bing Crosby. Now, Mills did that
Which picture was that?
The Big Broadcast of 1934.
Oh yeah? I didn't know about that.
Thomas - 101
See, Bing Crosby was the star. But we had played... The first theatre date that Bing Crosby played, we were the headliners, and Bing Crosby was the extra added attraction.
Where was that?
At the Paramount.
The Paramount. Cab Calloway was the headliner?

Yeah. And he had just made a name for himself on the radio, and he was like the extra added attraction. He just could walk on and off the stage. He'd just walk on there and sing. And that's how we got to know his brother. His brother was his manager.
He didn't care too much for Cab.
Hmm?
They had a little thing going against one another.
Maybe so. But he... Anyway, we got the job to make the picture with him.
Yeah, but after the picture...
Maybe so. Maybe so. Because Cab was kind of pushing him, and...
Right.
And we liked Bing, because we knew he was...
Thomas - 102
Well, Bing liked all of us, but he just didn't care too much for Cab.
Yeah, it's possible. A lot of people didn't care for Cab. Because Cab had a funny way about him. He was jealous of everybody...
It happened a little later, because I remember seeing... We made The Big Broadcast of 1936 with Eleanor Powell. Were you there?
Yeah, I was there.
...(?)..., that thing they show that every year on the air.
Oh, maybe I wasn't there. I don't know...
Illinois Jacquet was in that band, and I did that thing with...
[PAUSE]
